passages.text: When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place.
passages.sermon: The day of Pentecost arrived.\r\nAll the disciples were together.\r\nThey were in one place.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό

passages.text: Suddenly a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
passages.sermon:
The apostles and other believers gathered together in one place on the day of Pentecost.
Suddenly, a sound came from heaven.
The sound was like a strong, rushing wind.
The sound filled the entire house.
Everyone was sitting in the house when this happened.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι

passages.text: They saw tongues like flames of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.
passages.sermon:
The disciples sat together in one place on the day of Pentecost.
They saw something unusual.
They saw tongues that looked like fire.
These tongues separated from each other.
Each tongue rested on one person.
Every disciple received a tongue like fire.
passages.original: καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐφ’ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν

passages.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.
passages.sermon:
The people sat together in a house.
The Holy Spirit filled every person there.
Each person began to speak in other languages.
The Holy Spirit gave them the ability to speak these languages.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ Πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven.
passages.sermon: God-fearing Jews lived in Jerusalem.\r\nThese Jews were men.\r\nThey came from every nation under heaven.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: And when this sound rang out, a crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard them speaking his own language.
passages.sermon:
A sound rang out.
A crowd gathered.
The people in the crowd felt confused.
Each person heard the speakers use his own language.
passages.original: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθεν τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη ὅτι ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν

passages.text: Astounded and amazed, they asked, “Are not all these men who are speaking Galileans?
passages.sermon:
God-fearing Jews from every nation lived in Jerusalem.
A crowd heard a sound and gathered.
The people in the crowd were astounded and amazed.
They saw men speaking.
These men were Galileans.
The people asked, “Are not all these men who are speaking Galileans?”
passages.original: Ἐξίσταντο δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον λέγοντες Οὐχ ἰδοὺ πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι

passages.text: How is it then that each of us hears them in his own native language?
passages.sermon:
The crowd heard a loud sound.
Many people gathered together.
Each person heard the speakers in his own language.
The people were amazed.
They asked a question.
They said, “How can each of us hear them in our own native language?”
passages.original: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν

passages.text: Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; residents of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; visitors from Rome, both Jews and converts to Judaism; Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues!”
passages.sermon:
Many people were present in Jerusalem.
Some people came from Parthia.
Some people came from Media.
Some people came from Elam.
Some people lived in Mesopotamia.
Some people lived in Judea.
Some people lived in Cappadocia.
Some people lived in Pontus.
Some people lived in Asia.
Some people lived in Phrygia.
Some people lived in Pamphylia.
Some people came from Egypt.
Some people came from the parts of Libya near Cyrene.
Some people were visitors from Rome.
Some of these visitors were Jews.
Some of these visitors were converts to Judaism.
Some people were from Crete.
Some people were Arabs.
All these people heard the disciples speaking.
Each person heard the disciples speak in his own language.
The disciples spoke about the great things God had done.
Each person understood the wonders of God in his own tongue.
passages.original: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμῖται καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Astounded and perplexed, they asked one another, “What does this mean?”
passages.sermon:
A large crowd gathered in Jerusalem.
Many people came from different nations.
They saw and heard something amazing.
Everyone was astonished.
Everyone was confused.
People turned to each other.
They spoke to one another.
They asked, “What does this mean?”
passages.original: Ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ διηπόρουν ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι

passages.text: But others mocked them and said, “They are drunk on new wine!”
passages.sermon: Some people in the crowd mocked the disciples.\r\nThese people spoke with scorn.\r\nThey said, “They are drunk on new wine.”
passages.original: Ἕτεροι δὲ διαχλευάζοντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν

passages.text: Then Peter stood up with the Eleven, lifted up his voice, and addressed the crowd: “Men of Judea and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen carefully to my words.
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Peter stood up with the other eleven disciples.
Peter raised his voice.
Peter spoke to the people.
He spoke to the men of Judea.
He spoke to everyone living in Jerusalem.
Peter said, “Let this be known to you.”
Peter said, “Listen carefully to my words.”
passages.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἰερουσαλὴμ πάντες τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου

passages.text: These men are not drunk, as you suppose. It is only the third hour of the day!
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the crowd in Jerusalem.
Peter addressed the men of Judea and all who lived in Jerusalem.
Peter said, “These men are not drunk.
You suppose they are drunk.
It is only the third hour of the day.
The third hour means it is early in the morning.”
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας

passages.text: No, this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: ‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the crowd.
Peter referred to the prophet Joel.
Joel was a prophet of God.
Joel spoke about the last days.
God says, “In the last days, I will act.”
God says, “I will pour out My Spirit.”
God will pour out His Spirit on all people.
God’s Spirit will come to everyone.
Sons will prophesy.
Daughters will prophesy.
Young men will see visions.
Old men will dream dreams.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Ἰωήλ Καὶ ἔσται ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις λέγει ὁ Θεός ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν ὁράσεις ὄψονται καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὑμῶν ἐνυπνίοις ἐνυπνιασθήσονται

passages.text: Even on My menservants and maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the last days.
God says He will act in those days.
God has menservants and maidservants.
God will pour out His Spirit on His menservants.
God will pour out His Spirit on His maidservants.
God will do this in those days.
God’s menservants and maidservants will prophesy.
passages.original: καί‿ γε ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους μου καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας μου ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματός μου καὶ προφητεύσουσιν

passages.text: I will show wonders in the heavens above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and billows of smoke.
passages.sermon:
God will show wonders in the heavens above.
God will show signs on the earth below.
There will be blood.
There will be fire.
There will be billows of smoke.
passages.original: καὶ δώσω τέρατα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ σημεῖα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω αἷμα καὶ πῦρ καὶ ἀτμίδα καπνοῦ

passages.text: The sun will be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the coming of the great and glorious Day of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
God will act before the Day of the Lord comes.
The Day of the Lord will be great and glorious.
The sun will turn to darkness.
The moon will turn to blood.
These things will happen before the Day of the Lord arrives.
passages.original: ὁ ἥλιος μεταστραφήσεται εἰς σκότος καὶ ἡ σελήνη εἰς αἷμα πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν Κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ

passages.text: And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.’
passages.sermon:
God promises salvation.
He offers this to all people.
Anyone can receive it.
A person must call on the name of the Lord.
Everyone who calls on the Lord’s name will be saved.
passages.original: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ἐὰν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου σωθήσεται

passages.text: Men of Israel, listen to this message: Jesus of Nazareth was a man certified by God to you by miracles, wonders, and signs, which God did among you through Him, as you yourselves know.
passages.sermon:
Men of Israel, listen to this message.
Jesus came from Nazareth.
Jesus was a man.
God showed that Jesus was from Him.
God proved this to you.
God used miracles, wonders, and signs.
God did these things among you.
God did these things through Jesus.
You yourselves know this.
passages.original: Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τούτους Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον ἄνδρα ἀποδεδειγμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς δυνάμεσι καὶ τέρασι καὶ σημείοις οἷς ἐποίησεν δι’ αὐτοῦ ὁ Θεὸς ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν καθὼς αὐτοὶ οἴδατε

passages.text: He was delivered up by God’s set plan and foreknowledge, and you, by the hands of the lawless, put Him to death by nailing Him to the cross.
passages.sermon:
God had a set plan.
God knew what would happen beforehand.
God delivered Jesus up according to this plan.
You handed Jesus over to lawless men.
These lawless men nailed Jesus to the cross.
You put Jesus to death in this way.
passages.original: τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔκδοτον διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε

passages.text: But God raised Him from the dead, releasing Him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for Him to be held in its clutches.
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus from the dead.
God set Jesus free from the agony of death.
Death could not hold Jesus.
It was impossible for death to keep Jesus in its power.
passages.original: ὃν ὁ Θεὸς ἀνέστησεν λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου καθότι οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: David says about Him: ‘I saw the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
passages.sermon:
David is the speaker.
David speaks about Jesus.
David says, “I saw the Lord always before me.”
The Lord is always in front of David.
The Lord stands at David’s right hand.
Because the Lord is at David’s right hand, David will not be shaken.
passages.original: Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν Προορώμην τὸν Κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ

passages.text: Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell in hope, because You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
passages.sermon:
David speaks about the Lord.
David says his heart is glad.
David says his tongue rejoices.
David says his body will live in hope.
David trusts God.
David believes God will not abandon his soul to Hades.
David believes God will not let His Holy One see decay.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ηὐφράνθη μου ἡ καρδία καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μου ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ σάρξ μου κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ὅτι οὐκ ἐνκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μου εἰς ᾅδην οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν Ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν

passages.text: You have made known to me the paths of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence.’
passages.sermon:
God made the paths of life known to me.
God showed me how to live.
God will fill me with joy.
I will have joy when I am with God.
God’s presence brings me happiness.
passages.original: ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδοὺς ζωῆς πληρώσεις με εὐφροσύνης μετὰ τοῦ προσώπου σου

passages.text: Brothers, I can tell you with confidence that the patriarch David died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
passages.sermon:
David was a patriarch of Israel.
He died.
People buried David.
His tomb remains with us today.
I speak these things to you, brothers, with confidence.
passages.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου Δαυὶδ ὅτι καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ τὸ μνῆμα αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης

passages.text: But he was a prophet and knew that God had promised him on oath that He would place one of his descendants on his throne.
passages.sermon:
David was a prophet.
David knew something important.
God made a promise to David.
God swore an oath to David.
God promised to put one of David’s descendants on David’s throne.
passages.original: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that He was not abandoned to Hades, nor did His body see decay.
passages.sermon:
David was a prophet.
David saw what would happen in the future.
David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ.
David said that Christ was not abandoned to Hades.
David said that Christ’s body did not see decay.
passages.original: προϊδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὅτι οὔτε ἐνκατελείφθη εἰς ᾅδην οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν

passages.text: God has raised this Jesus to life, to which we are all witnesses.
passages.sermon: God raised Jesus to life.\r\nWe are all witnesses of this.
passages.original: Τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνέστησεν ὁ Θεός οὗ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες

passages.text: Exalted, then, to the right hand of God, He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus from the dead.
God exalted Jesus to His right hand.
Jesus received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father.
Jesus poured out the Holy Spirit.
You now see and hear the results of this.
passages.original: τῇ δεξιᾷ οὖν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑψωθεὶς τήν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐξέχεεν τοῦτο ὃ ὑμεῖς καὶ βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε

passages.text: For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” ’
passages.sermon:
David was a king of Israel.
David did not go up into heaven.
David himself spoke these words.
David said, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand.
Stay there until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’”
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ Δαυὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς λέγει δὲ αὐτός Εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου

passages.text: Therefore let all Israel know with certainty that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ!”
passages.sermon:
God acted.
God made Jesus both Lord and Christ.
You crucified Jesus.
All Israel must know this for certain.
passages.original: Ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι καὶ Κύριον αὐτὸν καὶ Χριστὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε

passages.text: When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
passages.sermon:
The people listened to Peter and the other apostles.
They heard that God made Jesus both Lord and Christ.
They understood that they had crucified Jesus.
Their hearts felt deep sorrow.
They spoke to Peter and the other apostles.
They said, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ κατενύγησαν τὴν καρδίαν εἶπόν τε πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους Τί ποιήσωμεν ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί

passages.text: Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the people.
Peter said, “Repent.
Each of you must be baptized.
Be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
God will forgive your sins.
You will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.”
passages.original: Πέτρος δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Μετανοήσατε φησίν Καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν καὶ λήμψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος

passages.text: This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off—to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself.”
passages.sermon:
God made a promise.
This promise belongs to you.
This promise also belongs to your children.
This promise belongs to all people who are far away.
The Lord our God will call some people to Himself.
This promise belongs to everyone whom God calls.
passages.original: ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς εἰς μακρὰν ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν

passages.text: With many other words he testified, and he urged them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the people.
He used many other words.
He gave strong testimony.
He urged the people.
He said, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”
passages.original: Ἑτέροις τε λόγοις πλείοσιν διεμαρτύρατο καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτοὺς λέγων Σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς ταύτης

passages.text: Those who embraced his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to the believers that day.
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to the people about Jesus.
Some people listened to Peter.
They accepted his message.
These people chose to believe in Jesus.
They were baptized.
About three thousand people joined the group of believers that day.
passages.original: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀποδεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθησαν καὶ προσετέθησαν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ψυχαὶ ὡσεὶ τρισχίλιαι

passages.text: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.
passages.sermon:
The believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching.
They devoted themselves to fellowship.
They devoted themselves to the breaking of bread.
They devoted themselves to prayer.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς

passages.text: A sense of awe came over everyone, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.
passages.sermon: Everyone felt awe.\r\nThe apostles performed many wonders.\r\nThe apostles performed many signs.
passages.original: Ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος πολλά τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο

passages.text: All the believers were together and had everything in common.
passages.sermon:
The believers trusted in Jesus.
All the believers gathered together.
They shared everything with each other.
No one kept things for themselves.
They lived as one community.
passages.original: Πάντες δὲ οἱ πιστεύοντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά

passages.text: Selling their possessions and goods, they shared with anyone who was in need.
passages.sermon:
The believers sold their possessions.
They sold their goods.
They shared what they had with everyone.
They gave to anyone who had a need.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν

passages.text: With one accord they continued to meet daily in the temple courts and to break bread from house to house, sharing their meals with gladness and sincerity of heart, praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.
passages.sermon:
The believers met together every day.
They gathered with one purpose.
They met in the temple courts.
They broke bread in different homes.
They shared their meals with glad hearts.
They were sincere in their hearts.
They praised God.
All the people liked them.
The Lord added new people to their group every day.
These new people were being saved.
passages.original: Καθ’ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ κλῶντές τε κατ’ οἶκον ἄρτον μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας αἰνοῦντες τὸν Θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν ὁ δὲ Κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό
